{"id":"persona-5s4b.52","title":"Pseudonym derivation has no scheme version, so the HKDF inputs can never be changed","description":"persona-core/src/pseudonym.rs:13-23 and persona-core/src/consumer.rs:47-68.

`derive_pseudonym(ikm, trust_domain, consumer_app_id)` feeds `consumer_app_id` directly as HKDF info and `trust_domain` directly as salt, with no version tag or protocol label anywhere in the input. Pseudonyms are the stable per-consumer identity a relying app keys its user records on (SpiffeId::pseudonymous, spiffe_id.rs:106-108). That makes the exact byte layout of these inputs a permanent wire commitment from the first release: any change — switching the info string, adding a field, moving to a different KDF — silently produces different pseudonyms and every downstream app sees all its users as new users, with no way to detect the change or to serve both schemes during a migration.

`ConsumerIdentity::selector_key()` (consumer.rs:47) is the other half: its per-variant format is documented (consumer.rs:39-46) as an implementation detail of a helper, but it is in fact the HKDF info input, so those seven format strings are equally frozen. Nothing in the doc says so, and a future contributor reformatting `unattested:uid:{uid}:pid:{pid}` would look like a cosmetic change.

Cheap fix now, impossible later: prefix the HKDF info with a scheme label and version, e.g. `persona-pseudonym-v1:{selector_key}`, and document on both functions that the inputs are a stable wire format bumped only by incrementing the version. This is a constraint (one fixed label) rather than a mechanism (no negotiation, no config) and it is the difference between a possible migration and an impossible one.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:58:50.938775511Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-13T20:58:50.938775511Z","labels":["risk","api-contract","versioning","review"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-5s4b.52","depends_on_id":"persona-5s4b","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:58:50.973622794Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}

new_value: Both fixed together in 5205a1c, since they are two halves of one API. .52: the HKDF info input is now prefixed with the fixed label persona-pseudonym-v1:, making a future scheme change expressible (v2 derives alongside v1 during a migration) rather than silent. One label, no negotiation, no config. ConsumerIdentity::selector_key's seven format strings are the other half of that commitment and were documented as an implementation detail of a helper; the doc now states they are a wire commitment and that changing one is a scheme change. .53: derive_pseudonym now takes &TrustDomain and &ConsumerIdentity -- types the crate already had -- so the salt/info swap is a type error instead of a well-formed wrong answer, and the unenforced convention that the caller pass selector_key() is gone. It returns [u8; 32] and is crate-private; the persona_core::derive_pseudonym re-export was dropped, which no caller outside persona-core used, applying the reasoning already recorded on derive_pseudonymous_id (HKDF over public inputs is not pseudonymity). SvidSigner::pseudonymous_id is now the only entry point. Test vectors recomputed from pyca/cryptography with the oracle recorded inline, preserving what persona-5s4b.69 flags as worth keeping; one test asserts the output differs from the same inputs derived without the label. Mutations verified: dropping the label, bumping the version, and swapping salt for info each kill tests.
